places.n: Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall
places.ad: 12 Tai Gin Road, Singapore 327874
places.w: Wan Qing Yuan, the 1880s villa off Balestier Road that Dr Sun Yat Sen used as his Southeast Asian base for the Tongmenghui — now a National Monument whose galleries tell how overseas Chinese communities bankrolled and shaped the 1911 Revolution. Anchor stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

places.n: Maha Sasana Ramsi Burmese Buddhist Temple
places.ad: 14 Tai Gin Road, Singapore 327873
places.w: Singapore's Burmese Buddhist temple, founded on Kinta Road in 1878 and rebuilt beside the Sun Yat Sen villa on Tai Gin Road in 1991 — it houses the largest white-marble Buddha outside Myanmar, carved from a single block of Mandalay marble. On the 'Faith, Film and Food' route of NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

places.n: Goh Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple & Wayang Stage
places.ad: 249 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: Balestier's red temple, founded in 1847 by Hokkien labourers on Joseph Balestier's sugar-cane estate ('Goh Chor' = Rochore), rebuilt in southern Chinese style in 1920/1928 — and beside it one of Singapore's last permanent wayang (Chinese opera) stages, built 1906 by Tan Boo Liat and still used by troupes during the Hungry Ghost Festival. Conserved by URA.
places.k: Temple + 1906 opera stage; performances in the 7th lunar month

places.ad: 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: The sole surviving rural-market building in Singapore, designed by local architect Kwan Yow Luen with animal-and-flower reliefs across its cream walls — a heritage-trail stop that still trades as a cluster of eateries. A planned April 2025 closure was reversed — the tenancy was extended by two years (Seth Lui, Feb 2025).

places.ad: Balestier Road, Singapore (to confirm at geocode)
places.w: An 18-storey 1986 apartment block whose stacked, Lego-like cubic modules — each home with its own terrace — were inspired by Moshe Safdie's Habitat 67 in Montreal: Balestier's modernist landmark, seen from the street.
places.k: Modernist residential landmark — view from outside

places.ad: Blocks 90-92 Whampoa Drive, Singapore
places.w: The 1973 hawker centre and wet market spread across HDB blocks 90, 91 and 92 on Whampoa Drive — successor to the old Rayman Market and a stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail. Two cooked-food halls side by side hold some of Balestier's best breakfasts: Hoover rojak, fish-head bee hoon, lor mee, Hokkien mee.
places.k: Hawker centre & wet market; most stalls morning to mid-afternoon

places.n: Former Malay Film Productions Studio (Shaw Studio)
places.ad: 8 Jalan Ampas, Singapore
places.w: Shaw Brothers' Malay Film Productions studio on Jalan Ampas (1947-1969), where more than 150 films — many starring P. Ramlee — were shot in the golden age of Malay cinema. The surviving studio gate and buildings sit at the end of a quiet lane off Balestier Road.
places.k: Heritage site — exterior only; on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail

places.ad: 230 & 246 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: 1950s Art Deco blocks built over former taro farmland and ponds, unusual among shophouses in housing a separate apartment on each floor — streamlined façades conserved with the pre-war shophouses along Balestier Road in 2003.
places.k: Conserved streetscape — view from Balestier Road

places.ad: Ah Hood Road / Jalan Rajah, Balestier, Singapore
places.w: A small green with an open lawn and pond, named for Dr Sun Yat Sen (Sun Zhongshan) — it faces the villa where he stayed, now the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.

places.ad: Whampoa Drive (near Block 85), Whampoa, Singapore
places.w: A 1973 dragon sculpture clad in broken China rice bowls, built as the centrepiece of a playground park behind Block 85 Whampoa; the park was cleared for the CTE in 1985 and the fountain stopped running after the 1980s, but the weathered dragon still coils by the expressway — one of Singapore's few surviving 1970s HDB-estate landmarks.

places.ad: 101 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: The open playing fields where five community clubs — the Indian Association, YMCA, Ceylon Sports Club and others — have shared grounds since the 1920s; the Ceylon Sports Club (est. 1928 from the 1920 Lanka Union) has its clubhouse here. Used as a Japanese Occupation vehicle dump, re-turfed by the clubs after 1945.
places.k: Club grounds — view from Balestier Road

places.ad: 360 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: Where Shaw Organisation's Hoover Theatre (opened 1960 at the Jalan Ampas junction, a cinema, live-show stage and even a church over 36 years) stood beside the President Theatre — both demolished in 1996 for today's Shaw Plaza-Twin Heights (1999), whose Balestier Cineplex kept the area's film thread alive; the Malay Film Productions studio is just down Jalan Ampas.

places.ad: 342 Balestier Road, Singapore 329774
places.w: Balestier's other chicken-rice institution (alongside Boon Tong Kee): founded in 1953 by Hainanese immigrants and run by three generations, everything made from scratch — silky steamed or crisp-skinned roast chicken over fluffy rice cooked in garlicky chicken broth, with chilli, dark soy and ginger paste. The Loy Kee Special Set is the full Hainanese spread on one tray.

places.ad: 639 Balestier Road, Singapore 329922
places.w: Balestier is Singapore's tau sar piah street, and Loong Fatt (since 1948) is its original — still in the same shophouse with the old tiled walls and floor, wooden tables and booths, baking flaky mung-bean pastries by hand. A stop on the National Heritage Board's Balestier Food Trail.

places.ad: 1 Thomson Road, #01-326, Balestier Hill Shopping Centre, Singapore 320002
places.w: A long-running zi char stall in the corner of a Balestier Hill coffeeshop, famous for its beef hor fun — silky rice-noodle sheets and tender beef in a fragrant black-bean gravy loaded with wok hei — the subject of Dr Leslie Tay's 'beef hor fun challenge'. Prawn paste chicken is the other order. Reviewers note consistency depends on who is at the wok.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-06, Singapore 320090
places.w: The long-famous Balestier rojak, now at Whampoa Food Centre and a repeat Michelin Bib Gourmand pick — a killer sauce of assam, fermented prawn paste and sugar tossed with crunchy jellyfish and creamy century egg alongside the usual fruit, you tiao and tau pok.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-32, Singapore 320090
places.w: You see the queue before the stall: a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) fried Hokkien mee that pairs thick bee hoon with yellow noodles in a slightly wet, umami-laden prawn stock. Open from mid-afternoon into the small hours, it is Whampoa's night-market anchor.

places.n: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-46, Singapore
places.w: Held the Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025, and widely called one of Singapore's best fish soups: sliced or fried fish-head bee hoon in a rich, milky stock finished with fried garlic. Morning hours only, a few days a week — go early.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-07, Singapore 320090
places.w: A former Michelin Bib Gourmand (2017) braised-duck stall: soy duck rice drenched in gravy, but regulars come for the velvety Cantonese-style duck porridge with a splash of braising gravy — 'you have never tasted duck porridge this good' (Miss Tam Chiak).

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore — stall unit to confirm at geocode
places.w: A one-dish Michelin-recognised stall: orh luak with just the right balance of egg and gooey starch, fried to crisp brown edges and served with a citrusy homemade chilli.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, Singapore — stall unit to confirm at geocode
places.w: A well-known Block 91 morning-market stall for handmade ban mian and noodle soups, loaded up with prawns, abalone clams, sliced fish, fish maw or pig's kidneys.

places.n: Mat Noh & Rose Authentic Ginger Fried Chicken Rice
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-27, Singapore
places.w: A Muslim-owned stall tucked into a far corner of Whampoa Makan Place that has achieved 'main character status' for one dish — crisp ginger-marinated fried chicken over rice.

places.n: Amoy St Lor Mee (Best Lu Mian In Town)
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-19, Singapore
places.w: Whampoa is almost synonymous with this stall and its bold claim to the 'Best Lu Mian In Town': a two-item menu of thick, starchy lor mee laden with ngoh hiang, fish nuggets and braised pork (or the amped-up Jumbo Meal), with long morning queues.

places.n: Xin Heng Feng Guo Tiao Tan
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-14/15, Singapore
places.w: A breakfast stalwart serving fishball kway teow and mee pok from 5am, switching to fish-head steamboat in the evening.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-34, Singapore
places.w: A carrot-cake stall carrying the Tanglin Halt name to Whampoa — picked by both Seth Lui's and Daniel Food Diary's Whampoa round-ups among the market's worth-queuing stalls.

places.ad: Balestier Plaza, 400 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A long-running North Indian kitchen in Balestier Plaza — butter chicken, fish curry, naan from the tandoor — that NHB's Balestier Food Trail lists among the road's food institutions and Eatbook names in its Balestier guide.

places.n: Kai Juan (Ah Hak) Bak Kut Teh
places.ad: Kai Juan Coffeeshop, 395/397 Balestier Road, Singapore (exact unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Half a century of Teochew-style bak kut teh — a clear, moderately peppery broth over pork ribs, with rice and salted vegetables for about $7.50 — in a coffeeshop of rusty gates, granite floors and wooden tables that still looks 1970s. A stop on NHB's Balestier Food Trail.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-67, Singapore 320090
places.w: Whampoa's nasi lemak stall, named in Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls and HungryGoWhere's Whampoa Food Centre guide (a 'Hi Leskmi Whampoa Nasi Lemak' branch also trades at One Punggol).

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-28, Singapore 320091
places.w: Min jiang kueh, the folded griddle pancake, as a Whampoa breakfast stop — on Daniel Food Diary's 10 Whampoa breakfast stalls and Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-10, Singapore 320091
places.w: An early-morning steamed dim sum stall, headlined in Daniel Food Diary's Whampoa breakfast guide and listed in Eatbook's Whampoa Market round-up.

places.n: Yu Chu La Mian Xiao Long Bao (Whampoa)
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-45, Singapore 320091
places.w: Hand-pulled noodles and soup dumplings made at the stall — HungryGoWhere's Whampoa pick, also in Eatbook's Whampoa Market list.

places.ad: 586 Balestier Road, #01-01, Singapore
places.w: The Balestier branch of the famous Old Airport Road lor mee, with an extended menu: thick starchy gravy over flat noodles, topped with deep-fried cod nuggets ($10 signature) — in Eatbook's Balestier guide and reviewed by Live2Makan.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-21, Singapore 320091
places.w: Yong tau foo served in laksa gravy (about $4) — a Whampoa crossover named by City Nomads, TheSmartLocal and Seth Lui.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-36, Singapore (block to confirm)
places.w: A morning-only stall (about 6.30am to 12.30pm, Tue-Sun) deep-frying radish cake until crisp outside and soft within — in City Nomads', Eatbook's, TheSmartLocal's and HungryGoWhere's Whampoa guides. Its owner Mr Lim has sold carrot cake in stick form for over two decades (Women's Weekly).

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore (unit to confirm)
places.w: Whampoa's mee siam specialist — on both Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls and HungryGoWhere's 15 can't-miss Whampoa stalls.

places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore (unit to confirm)
places.w: Shaved ice, pandan jelly, coconut milk and gula Melaka — the Whampoa chendol named by both Eatbook and HungryGoWhere.

places.ad: Balestier Plaza (level 2), 400 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm)
places.w: The viral hole-in-the-wall on Balestier Plaza's second floor: wok-kissed Hokkien mee and homemade kaya toast that Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost: 'local breakfast done right') and Miss Tam Chiak have all written up — it has since spawned outlets in Holland Village (Jun 2025) and Fortune Centre (Dec 2025).

places.ad: 611 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: The cult handmade-bun family business, at its Balestier outlet — Time Out went inside to see how 'Singapore's best handmade buns' are made, and HungryGoWhere interviewed the family on the dying art of handmade baos.

places.ad: 328 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: A family coffee roaster since 1950 selling Nanyang-style kopi powder — beans from Indonesia roasted the traditional way with sugar and margarine (the Legacy Blend keeps the founding recipe). On NHB's Balestier Food Trail; Makansutra profiled its revival.

places.n: Ah Hui Big Prawn Noodle (Balestier Food Centre) — CLOSED
places.ad: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-13, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: Aromatic, umami-rich prawn noodle soup — a slightly sweet, garlicky prawn stock, firm big prawns and optional tender pork ribs ($5) — the headline stall of Balestier's heritage market building in both Seth Lui's and Women's Weekly's Balestier Food Centre guides.

pv.ss: Seth Lui May 2023 + MustShareNews: Balestier Market stall's last day 13 Jul 2023 (rent/health); re-checked 2026-10-03

places.n: Soon Kee Long House Boneless Duck Rice (Balestier Food Centre)
places.ad: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: Teochew braised duck rice ($5.50) under thick slabs of boneless duck, cucumber, boiled peanuts and a fragrant braising sauce — picked by Seth Lui and Women's Weekly at Balestier Food Centre.

places.n: Miao Sin Popiah & Carrot Cake — CLOSED
places.ad: Balestier Market & Food Centre, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: CLOSED 26 Feb 2026. Ong Chin Quay's 45-year-old popiah and carrot-cake stall (started 1980 on Upper Boon Keng Road, at Balestier Market since the 2010s) shut when the 72-year-old hawker found no successor (Mothership; Seth Lui). Women's Weekly had named it among Balestier Food Centre's best and Singapore's great popiah stops. Kept here, flagged, as part of the market's record.

pv.ss: Mothership / Seth Lui: last day 26 Feb 2026

places.n: Whampoa Soya Bean & Grass Jelly Drinks
places.ad: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-52, Singapore 320091
places.w: A second-generation stall in the same spot since 1979 (family business from 1968), making silky tau huay and soya milk — written up by Dr Leslie Tay ('smooth as silk') and Daniel Food Diary, and named in City Nomads' Whampoa guide; DFD notes its inclusion in the MICHELIN Guide.

places.ad: 556 Balestier Road, Singapore
places.w: The Balestier flagship of Whampoa Keng, famous for charcoal fish-head steamboat in a rich broth plus zi char dishes — chronicled by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost: the 'one man, two wives' story and the new flagship) and reviewed again by Live2Makan in Aug 2025.

places.ad: 365/369 Balestier Road, Singapore 329785
places.w: A 24-hour bak kut teh house run by three generations of the Yap family since 1966; whole blocks of sugarcane go into the peppery Teochew broth — a nod to Balestier's sugar-plantation past. On Seth Lui's 18 best bak kut teh (Oct 2024) and Eatbook's best bak kut teh list.

places.ad: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-18, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: Battered, deep-fried ripe banana alongside jackfruit, green bean, sweet potato and tapioca fritters — and a nian gao-and-yam goreng for about $1 — on Seth Lui's and Women's Weekly's Balestier Food Centre lists.

places.n: Bugis Street Chuen Chuen Chicken Rice (Balestier Food Centre)
places.ad: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-12, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
places.w: A simple, wallet-friendly chicken rice — juicy chicken on fragrant rice with cucumber and soup — named by Seth Lui and Women's Weekly at Balestier Food Centre.

places.ad: VIIO @ Balestier, 520 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm)
places.w: The Taipei beef-noodle shop recognised by the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand in Taipei opened its first overseas outlet here on 13 Feb 2023 — a modern take on Taiwanese braised beef noodles (Seth Lui, Eatbook, Miss Tam Chiak, HungryGoWhere).

places.ad: 399/401/403 Balestier Road
places.w: A chicken rice institution since 1979; promoted to Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.
